title: Render provenance and citation markers as grouped icon asides
description:
Supersedes #166. Closes #148 (default shinychat citation UI) and closes #149 (minimal markers) — the look #149 asked for, through the mechanism #148 asked for. ## Where things stand Both PRs chase the same destination: small icon markers instead of pills, with a one-shot pulse on mount. #166 gets there with commons-owned CSS that restyles shinychat's compact-aside DOM state by state; this PR gets there by changing what commons *asks shinychat to render* — labeled identity asides — and confining commons CSS to shinychat's public `--shiny-chat-aside-marker-*` theming variables. How they compare, at a glance: | | #166 | This PR | |---|---|---| | Marker look | Small icon, pulse on mount | Same look (warning icon identical to #166's; citation quote mark redrawn as a fixed path) | | Mechanism | CSS overrides of shinychat's compact-aside DOM | shinychat's aside grouping + public theme variables | | Multiple citations in one paragraph | Flattened to one dot, indistinguishable from a single citation | One marker with a "+N" overflow count and a carousel popover; every citation stays reachable | | Hover/focus/expanded states | Re-implemented per tone in commons CSS | Inherited from shinychat | | Cited answers in review transcript | Marker removed | Unchanged here; see note below | ## What this PR does Conceptually, three moves: - **Citations render as labeled identity asides** instead of compact numbered chips, so shinychat owns the marker entirely — grouping, overflow counts, popovers, and interaction states. - **All three markers (Verified, Untrusted, citation) render icon-only.** The label stays in the DOM for the pill's `aria-label`, and commons CSS touches only shinychat's public `--shiny-chat-aside-marker-*` variables. - **Singleton citation popovers gain a body title** (icon + source label), since shinychat only renders its own title row for grouped asides. A local example app renders every outcome — including a three-citation paragraph and a singleton citation — for manual comparison against the review transcript. It's not part of the package; source below.
Example app: all provenance outcomes and grouped citations ```r # Save as app.R and run with shiny::runApp(). # # What a live commons chat renders for each provenance outcome: # Verified and Untrusted answers end with a marker; Cited answers show # their citation asides instead — including a paragraph with several # citations, which shinychat accumulates into one marker with a "+N" # overflow and a carousel popover. A fourth message carries a lone # citation: shinychat only renders its popover title row for grouped # asides, so commons puts its own title (icon + source label) at the # top of the aside body to keep singleton popovers named too. corpus <- list( list( label = "documentation", kind = "prose", text = "Revenue excludes tax and shipping." ), list( label = "sales table", kind = "schema", text = "Revenue is recognized at shipment, not at order placement." ), list( label = "measure definitions", kind = "definition", text = "Gross margin is net revenue minus cost of goods sold." ) ) citation <- function(quote, explanation) { render_citation_aside(quote, explanation, corpus)$html } ui <- bslib::page_fillable( theme = commons_theme(), shinychat::chat_ui( "chat", messages = list( list( role = "assistant", content = paste( "6 orders came in last week.", provenance_aside("A") ) ), list( role = "assistant", content = paste( "Revenue excludes tax and shipping, is recognized at shipment,", "and feeds straight into gross margin.", citation( "Revenue excludes tax and shipping.", "Supports the definition given in the answer." ), citation( "Revenue is recognized at shipment, not at order placement.", "Supports the recognition timing." ), citation( "Gross margin is net revenue minus cost of goods sold.", "Supports the margin description." ) ) ), # A lone citation: shinychat only renders its popover title row # for grouped asides, so the aside body carries its own title # (icon + source label) to name the source here too. list( role = "assistant", content = paste( "Revenue is recognized at shipment, not at order placement.", citation( "Revenue is recognized at shipment, not at order placement.", "Supports the recognition timing." ) ) ), list( role = "assistant", content = paste( "Margins appear roughly flat. Treat this as an estimate.", provenance_aside("C") ) ) ) ) ) server <- function(input, output, session) {} shiny::shinyApp(ui, server) ```
## Notes - **Icon concepts are #166's, with glyphs from Radix Icons (MIT).** The warning mark is a white exclamation on the original yellow circle, matching #166. The citation mark is a "quote" glyph in white on a navy tile — #166's serif `"` text element was white-on-transparent, designed to sit on a solid dot, and its metrics shifted with font substitution; the redraw is a fixed ``. The trusted mark is a "check" glyph in white on the green shield badge. - **Citations deliberately don't pulse.** Verified and Untrusted keep #166's one-shot pulse (disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`); the pulse should say "check this answer's provenance," not "this answer cites something." - **Cited answers keep their review marker here; #166 removes it.** Live chat shows no Cited marker in either PR — the citation asides are the signal. But review transcripts don't recreate inline citations today, so removing the marker there would leave Cited answers indistinguishable from answers with no data activity. Worth revisiting once the (forthcoming) sibling replay PR lands citation asides in review. ## Validation Unit tests updated and passing (`test-citations.R`, `test-provenance.R`). Browser tests updated for the new markup and passing (`test-citation-browser.R`, 27 expectations against live chromote). Manual check of the example app above recommended for glyph placement, the stadium shape on grouped markers, pulse timing, and dark mode (tone hexes were chosen for light backgrounds).

Adopt shinychat's page_chat(): replace commons_ui() with commons_theme()
description:
shinychat's new [`page_chat()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/shinychat/pull/329) owns page composition, which left `commons_ui()` — our thin `chat_ui()` wrapper that attached commons's CSS/JS — with no way to get those assets onto the page. This PR removes `commons_ui()` and moves asset delivery into `commons_theme()`, an ordinary bslib theme that works with `page_chat()` or any bslib page. `commons_server()` is unchanged.

The encouraged pattern for a commons app is now plain shinychat UI plus the theme:

```r
library(shiny)
library(shinychat)

ui <- page_chat("Assistant", id = "chat", theme = commons_theme())

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  agent <- commons(
    ellmer::chat_anthropic(),
    data_sources = data_source(sales = sales)
  )
  commons_server("chat", agent)
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

For an embedded chat, use `chat_ui()` inside any bslib page with the same `theme = commons_theme()`; `inst/app.R` is a complete example.

One thing worth knowing when reviewing: theme dependencies render *before* shinychat's own stylesheet, so commons's `.shiny-chat-*` overrides needed strictly higher specificity (or, where shinychat exposes a theme variable, moving to the variable instead). Caught via live browser testing; details are in the CSS and `commons_theme()`.

Commit walkthrough:

- e85af0b — add `commons_theme()`.
- 978b4f1 — remove `commons_ui()`; port `commons_app()`, the trajectory reviewer, examples, tests, and docs.
- a1e566f — drop `icon_assistant = HTML("")`; shinychat now omits the icon by default ([#345](https://github.com/posit-dev/shinychat/pull/345)).
- e934e97 — drop explicit `enable_cancel`/`allow_attachments`; `NULL` defers to `chat_server()` ([#264](https://github.com/posit-dev/shinychat/pull/264)).
- 45bee16 — serve the icon SVGs from the `commons-chat` dependency instead of a registered resource path.
- d20d254 — move bslib/htmltools/sass to Imports (already transitive via shinychat).
- 9123484 — drop a redundant example app; `inst/app.R` covers the pattern.

Verified: the four affected test files pass, and the example apps were exercised live in a browser with a real agent (assets load via the theme, pills/tool rows render with commons styling, icons serve 200). The full suite and shinytest2 tests were too slow locally — relying on CI for those.

title: ci: Add the Python release workflow and publishing metadata
description: ## Summary Reserving `posit-commons` on PyPI needs a real release, because PyPI has no reservation mechanism and a pending trusted publisher does not hold a name either. This adds the workflow that does it: `py-release.yaml` publishes `pkg-py` on `py-v*` tags through trusted publishing. The first upload goes through a pending publisher, so no API token is ever created and none has to be revoked afterwards. That replaces the token-then-revoke sequence recorded in the tracking issue. A guard between build and publish fails the run if the tag disagrees with the built version. PyPI does not allow re-uploading a version to correct it, so a mismatch would be permanent. ## Notes for the reviewer The license and project URL metadata is outside the stated scope of reserving the name. It is here because `0.1.0.dev0` becomes a permanent public artifact the moment it uploads, and the current metadata declares no license at all. The license text is a per-package copy, matching what `pkg-r/` already does. The release job has no GitHub environment gate. Anyone able to push a `py-v*` tag can publish, and tag pushes are not covered by branch protection. This was deferred rather than rejected, since adding an environment later is a one-field edit on the PyPI publisher config. Say so if you want it in place before the first release. `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` is pinned to the mutable `release/v1` ref, consistent with the `@v6` pins on the existing actions in this repo. Before any tag is pushed, the pending publisher has to exist on PyPI: project `posit-commons`, owner `posit-dev`, repository `commons`, workflow `py-release.yaml`, no environment. Version stays at `0.1.0.dev0`. Note that a plain `pip install posit-commons` does install it, verified after publishing: resolvers only skip pre-releases when there is a stable version to prefer, and there is not one yet. The pre-release marking starts doing its job at the first stable release. ## Manual actions I created a "pending publisher" on my account on PyPI: Once the package is created, I'll add @simonpcouch and @cpsievert as backup owners to limit bus factor. ## Testing `pkg-py` checks are green (ruff, pyrefly, pytest) and `uv sync --locked` still resolves against the unchanged lockfile. Both artifacts build, `twine check` passes on each, and the wheel installs into a clean 3.11 venv with the expected name split and the new metadata present. The tag guard was exercised by hand against three tag spellings: it accepts `py-v0.1.0.dev0` and rejects `py-v0.1.0` and `py-v0.1.0-dev0`. The publish workflow itself cannot run until a tag is pushed. Tracked locally as kata `4t9b`.

title: feat: Add citation normalization and matching to the Python package
description:
## Summary

This PR adds citation normalization and matching to the Python implementation, via the `commons._citations` module (the equivalent of `R/citations.R`). The normalization rules and the matching verdicts are shared, live in `tests/shared/citations.json`, and both the Python and R suites run the same contract.

The Python implementation uses a `CorpusEntry` dataclass to hold an immutable record of one trusted passage a quote can be checked against, holding the passage itself (`text`), a reader-facing `label` that names its source in the rendered aside, and a `kind` of `"prose"`, `"definition"` or `"schema"` saying which layer it came from.

## Changes affecting R

`pkg-r/tests/testthat/test-citations.R` loses two hand-written tests, `"citation matching forgives reflowed whitespace and typography"` and `"trivial quotes cannot promote an answer"`. Both stated expectations the Python suite also needs, so they move into the shared fixture using the machinery from #163. Three fixture-driven tests replace them, covering the normalization rules, the matching verdicts, and the minimum quote length.

## Shared-fixture guidance

`AGENTS.md` and `tests/shared/README.md` are updated in this PR to clarify that the shared fixtures should govern behavior a user can observe rather than specific implementation detail. The goal here is that each package should implement idiomatically in its own language.

## Testing

The fixture holds 12 normalization cases and 11 matching cases, including both guards: the 10-character minimum, tested at its boundary and with a case proving it counts the normalized form rather than the raw input, and the rule that only the quote is ever verified, which is structural here since `match_citation()` takes a quote and a corpus and nothing else. Both suites enumerate those cases.

title: feat: Implement provenance in Python behind a shared fixture
description:
## Summary

Adds `derive_provenance_tag()` and the provenance display copy to the Python package as `commons._provenance`, with `Tag` as an enum rather than bare strings. 

The truth table and the display strings are behavior both packages must agree on, so they live in `tests/shared/provenance.json` and both suites enumerate the same cases rather than each restating them. The R suite reads a generated copy, because testthat needs its fixtures inside the package and an installed package cannot reach the repository root. `scripts/sync-shared-fixtures.sh` produces that copy and a new `verify-shared-fixtures` workflow re-runs the script and fails when the committed copy is stale.

## Notes for the reviewer

**This PR touches R code.** This PR lands the first shared fixture and the mechanism around it. That mechanism is the deliverable to weigh most on the R side.

Python notes:

**`Tag` is a `StrEnum`, not a plain `str, Enum` mixin.** That mixin formats as `"Tag.A"`, while R writes the bare letter to the `commons.provenance.tag` span attribute. An f-string would have produced Python traces the R trajectory reviewer cannot match, and nothing would have errored. There is a test pinning `str(Tag.A) == "A"`.

**`pkg-py/pyproject.toml` gains `search-path` for pyrefly.** `tests` is a package rooted at `pkg-py/`, not under `src/`, so the import between test modules did not resolve and `py-check` would have failed. Worth knowing for future work: running `pyrefly` from inside a `.worktrees/` checkout reports a false pass, because it silently omits `tests/` whenever any ancestor directory name begins with a dot. Verified by reproducing the same tree at a path with and without a dot-directory. Local type checking of test files has to happen somewhere outside `.worktrees/`.

**`AGENTS.md` gains a writing rule, and this branch applies it.** Neither package is a port of the other, so the Python package's docstring, its PyPI `description`, and the kata section no longer say it is. Only the docstring came from this branch; the other two predate it, and landing the rule while leaving them would have contradicted it on arrival. Instances of "port" that describe R code carried over from data-dict are left alone, since those are accurate and describe the opposite direction.

**`provenance_aside()` has no Python counterpart.** It has no caller there yet, and depends on icon resolution that does not exist there either.

The fixture only covers tags a tool can actually set. `pkg-r/R/tools.R` emits A and B; C is derived and never an input, so no case feeds it in. Both runners assert the case list is non-empty, because a truncated fixture would otherwise enumerate nothing and pass.

## Testing

ruff, pyrefly, and pytest pass on Python 3.11 and 3.13. The two new R tests pass against the real `R/provenance.R`.

I checked that the fixture actually governs both languages rather than just sitting beside them: renaming one display label in the source makes the R test fail, the Python test fail, and the sync check go dirty.

Full `R CMD check` was not run locally, since commons' Imports are not installed here. CI covers it.

One non-blocking observation, not addressed here: `MIGRATING.md:53` enumerates the CI workflows as a complete list, and has been out of date since #161 added `py-release`.

title: Scaffold the Python package in pkg-py/
description:
## Summary
`pkg-py/` becomes a real installable package instead of the placeholder that landed in #146: hatchling build backend, `src/commons/` with a `py.typed` marker, a `[tracing]` extra, and a dev group of pytest, ruff, and pyrefly. It exports nothing yet, so `commons.__all__` is empty and there is no public API to review.

## Notes for the reviewer

**The Python floor is 3.11, and the CI matrix moves with it.** Initial planning had the floor at 3.10 to match shinychat, but `raghilda` 0.2.0 requires `>=3.11,<3.14`, so we'll be limited by that requirement.

`requires-python` mirrors that `<3.14` cap, so the metadata does not claim Pythons the package cannot install on. 3.14 is the current stable release, and without the cap the two installers disagreed there: pip refused with an error naming raghilda, a package the user never asked for, while uv ignored raghilda's cap and installed it on 3.14.7 regardless. Both now name `posit-commons`. An upper bound does propagate to consumers and needs a release to withdraw, so removal is tracked against posit-dev/raghilda#93, which reports raghilda's own checks passing unchanged on 3.14. The CI matrix is 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13, which is every version the package supports.

**The placeholder test is replaced rather than deleted.** `tests/test_packaging.py` pins the distribution/import name split, which is the one part of this scaffold that can regress without anyone noticing: hatchling infers the package directory from the distribution name, so `posit-commons` makes it look for `src/posit_commons/` and fail, and renaming the directory silences that error while quietly changing what consumers import. The test fails on that rename.

**`py-check` gained a type-check step, using pyrefly.** py-shiny has made pyrefly its default type gate and marked pyright for removal, so a greenfield package should start there instead of migrating later, and it drops the Node dependency pyright's PyPI wrapper carries.

One behavioural difference is worth knowing before writing the pydantic models in M2. pyrefly reads a model's `extra` setting where pyright assumes a fixed synthesized `__init__`, so on a default `extra="ignore"` model an unknown keyword is not reported, because pydantic accepts and discards it at runtime. Models that should reject unknown keys need `extra="forbid"`, which the dictionary reader wants regardless so that a `data-dict.yaml` typo fails at construction. pyrefly flags the typo there, inherited config included.

The `pkg-py/README.md` fixture sentence is corrected too. Adding `readme = "README.md"` sends that file to PyPI as the long description, where a repo-relative link resolves to nothing, and the sentence also claimed this suite reads `tests/shared/` in place, which is ruled out in favour of sync-and-verify and is impossible for an installed package anyway.

## Testing

`uv sync --locked --all-extras`, `ruff check`, `pyrefly check`, and `pytest` all pass on both 3.11 and 3.13, so CI's `--locked` will not trip on a stale lock. pyrefly needs a `[tool.pyrefly]` section to resolve imports and reports nothing without one, so it was checked against a deliberate bad return and an unknown keyword on an `extra="forbid"` model: both are caught, it exits non-zero, and the clean tree exits zero. It is a real gate, not a step that passes by doing nothing. Separately, the built wheel installed into a clean 3.11 environment imports as `commons`, reports `posit-commons` through `importlib.metadata`, and raises `ModuleNotFoundError` on `import posit_commons`, which is the consumer-facing behaviour the packaging tests assert against an editable install.

title: Restructure as an R + Python monorepo
description:
Moves the R package from the repository root into `pkg-r/`, adds a `pkg-py/` skeleton, and establishes `tests/shared/` for cross-language spec fixtures. Implements kata `z26z` / M1 Task 0 of the Python port plan (decision D7).

**Includes three kata-config commits alongside the restructure**, adding `.kata.toml`, a kata section in `AGENTS.md`, and one `.gitignore` entry. They are independent of the move and touch three files in total.

## Why one repository

commons' behavior lives substantially in artifacts that have to agree across both languages: the system prompt, the citation dialect and its guards, the provenance truth table and its display copy, and the tracing span contract. In separate repositories each of those is a copy that drifts silently, and prompt drift fails invisibly, since nothing errors and the agent simply behaves differently in one language. `tests/shared/` is where those contracts become fixtures CI enforces instead of prose that rots. The precedent is [posit-dev/shinychat](https://github.com/posit-dev/shinychat).

## Reviewing this

The first commit is a pure relocation, verifiable rather than taken on trust: `git show --stat -M` reports `172 files changed, 0 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-)`. The remaining commits are each a single concern (CI scoping, install instructions, root scaffolding, docs), so reviewing commit by commit is much easier than reading the squashed diff.

The repository is knowingly broken at the first commit, since the workflows still point at root-relative paths until the third.

## Things a reviewer could not infer from the diff

- **The move silently broke five `.gitignore` patterns.** A pattern containing an internal separator is anchored to the directory of the file declaring it, so `inst/resources/`, `inst/tiles/`, `inst/pkgs`, `inst/hex/output` and `src/*.{o,so,dll}` all stopped matching once the package moved. The failure is quiet: compiled objects and generated asset directories just become committable. Fixed by splitting package-relative patterns into `pkg-r/.gitignore` and leaving only separator-free patterns at the root, where they match at any depth and so cover `pkg-py/` too. `*.Rcheck/` and `*.tar.gz` are also now ignored, which they never were before the split.
- **Two workflows needed changes that the issue does not mention.** `deploy.yml` pushed `path: inst` to Connect and would have kept reporting success while deploying a path that no longer exists; it now uses `pkg-r/inst` and has a `paths:` filter so a Python-only PR cannot trigger an R deploy. `citation-browser.yaml` runs `devtools::test()` and needed the same working-directory treatment as `R CMD check`.
- **`defaults.run.working-directory` does not apply to `uses:` steps**, so the r-lib actions take their own `working-directory` input. `R-CMD-check` has no `run:` steps and therefore no job default at all. pkgdown's deploy step keeps `folder: pkg-r/docs` spelled from the repository root, because the JamesIves action resolves it there rather than from the job's working directory.
- **`NEWS.md` does not exist**, despite being named in the issue's move list.
- **The `subdir` sweep was two occurrences**, not the wider sweep across vignettes and `inst/skills/` the issue anticipated. Spelled as pak's path form `posit-dev/commons/pkg-r` rather than `subdir = "pkg-r"`, which is `remotes::install_github()`'s argument.

## Deliberate departures

- **`pkg-py/` is not empty.** The task asks for py-check green against an empty directory, which is not possible: `uv sync` needs a `pyproject.toml` and `pytest` exits 5 on a suite with no tests. It carries a placeholder `pyproject.toml` (`package = false`) and one placeholder test, both of which the scaffold task deletes. A workflow green because it does nothing would be worse than no workflow.
- **`LICENSE` and `LICENSE.md` are duplicated** at the root and in `pkg-r/`. `R CMD check` resolves the `DESCRIPTION` reference inside the package, and GitHub only detects a repository license at the root.
- **Split into 12 commits** rather than the single commit the task specifies, so each is independently reviewable.

## Needs a repository admin, not a code change

`paths:` filters mean a required status check that never runs stays pending forever under branch protection and blocks the merge. If any R check is currently required, that setting needs adjusting before this lands.

## Verification

py-check verified locally: `uv sync --locked`, `ruff`, `pytest` all pass. `R CMD build` from `pkg-r/` produces a valid tarball and the structural checks the move could have broken (`DESCRIPTION` located, namespace information) pass.

`R CMD check` and the pkgdown build could not be completed locally, since none of the package's twelve hard dependencies are installed in the available R library. That is the one item this PR cannot self-certify, and CI covers it.

This branch was rebased onto three commits that landed upstream after it was written (`#132`, `#138`, `#145`). Those added five new files under `R/` and `tests/testthat/`, which git's directory-rename detection folded into the relocation commit; all 27 files those commits touched are byte-identical to `main` inside `pkg-r/`.

## Not included

`tests/shared/` holds only the contract describing what belongs there. Fixtures land as the provenance and citation code is ported, together with the R-side runner. The Python package itself is the next task.

Shared *shipped* artifacts are also out of scope here and decided separately as plan D10: the system prompt moves to a root `prompts/` source in M5 and the browser assets to a root `www/` in M8, each synced into both packages with CI failing on a stale copy. Worth knowing because neither an R package nor a Python wheel can ship a file from outside its own directory, so sharing always means a generated copy rather than a direct read. That is also why `tests/shared/README.md` describes the R suite as consuming a synced copy.

`MIGRATING.md` covers what a developer used to R tooling at the repository root needs to change. It should be removed at a later date once we're all comfortable with the monorepo.

description:

Treat a connection to Snowflake/Databricks plus a schema path as minimally sufficient:

```
db <- DBI::dbConnect(odbc::snowflake())

source <- data_source(
  db,
  options = data_source_options(
    include = DBI::Id(...)
  )
)

agent <- commons(chat_anthropic(), source)
```

commons then discovers the schema and native semantic models without requiring a data dictionary.

description:
The last pieces of the Snowflake/Databricks integration for now. Closes #55, related to #86.
Write-up from Codex

Step 7 completed semantic scoping and runtime context. Native models now retain canonical dependency identities, public members, relationships, filters, facts, and scoped context. Associated-model discovery requires the full selected dependency closure. Review tightened canonical deduplication, unresolved-relation handling, and Snowflake fact/filter exposure. Step 8 added bounded lazy catalog discovery. Broad selections retain lightweight relation manifests, switch to `search_catalog` when prompt content is large, apply exclusions before limits, and hydrate columns on first description. Review bounded candidate hydration and Snowflake semantic-view hydration before metadata reads. Step 9 hardened authority boundaries. Sources snapshot warehouse identity, roles, and namespace; governed operations reject changed sessions. Exact relations, authored dictionaries, and native models require zero-row queryability checks. Authorization failures are cached while transient and unknown failures retry. Review identified Snowflake fact-only probes, exact-relation classification, secondary roles, missing SQLSTATE handling, and missing-table diagnostics. The final design separates discovery state from relation kind so `hive_metastore` objects with unknown kinds remain valid. Step 10 added typed native parameters and exact trusted queries. Snowflake variables and verified queries and Databricks metric-view parameters are imported without merging them into data-dict definitions. A separate calculation registry validates scalar types, binds values through DBI, quotes only allowlisted identifiers, and marks results trusted only after successful execution. Review tightened integer precision, temporal validation, unsupported-model handling, and optional live coverage for native parameter and verified-query assets. Real Snowflake and Databricks connections exercised exact and namespace discovery, session changes, associated semantic models where available, lazy hydration, compiled definitions, and typed DBI-bound calculations. Dedicated roles, denied objects, parameterized native models, and verified-query views remain opt-in because those assets are not configured in the current environments. The implementation favored adapter-owned parsing and SQL generation, with only typed argument validation and calculation execution shared across backends. It does not parse arbitrary SQL to infer dependencies or trust.

title: Restore Shinychat ownership of verified citation display
description:
This PR restores the boundary originally established in #107: Commons is responsible for server-side citation verification and audit records; Shinychat is responsible for client-side citation display and interaction.

[Shinychat#326](https://github.com/posit-dev/shinychat/pull/326) adds compact asides (i.e., superscripts), letting Commons request and style compact citations through supported display and CSS APIs rather than reconstructing citation UI with custom markup and private selectors.

## Behavior

- Verified citations render as compact numbered references, with the source label and icon available in the popover and accessible name.
- Citation streaming preserves surrounding Markdown whitespace.
- Commons records citation decisions in the answer audit trail, and trajectory review replays those recorded decisions.

## Verification

Citation scanner and trajectory-review tests cover projection and replay. Browser tests cover streamed compact citations, source-aware markers, and popovers.

Closes #123.

* `evaluation.md` - Guidance on creating evals. This is almost entirely pulled from the eval notes in #47 and #46 and the work in https://github.com/posit-dev/devrel-agent. I would expect this to change a lot. I'm mostly including it as a placeholder so we can figure out the organization of the skill/references. 

Also adds some general principles to `SKILL.md`. 

I have not thoroughly tested this by creating a new agent (I did one quick pass, but it was very basic). I would expect things to shift and change once we do so, but I thought it might be helpful to review at this stage anyway.

Closes #47

title: Verify citations in-stream and record answer provenance for trajectory review
description:
## Summary

This PR reworks how a commons answer's trustworthiness travels from the model to the user, and
from the user's session to the audit trail. The verification logic itself isn't new — quotes
were already exact-matched against the corpus on the server. What changes is the architecture
around it, in two ways:

1. **What the user sees is now authored by the server.** Citation markup is verified and
   rewritten *while the answer streams*, so only server-authored elements ever reach the
   browser. The client-side retrofit protocol is gone.
2. **What the reviewer sees is now recorded, not reconstructed.** Each answer's trust verdict
   and citation decisions are written to the trace at the moment they're made, and
   `trajectory_review()` plays them back verbatim instead of re-deriving them heuristically.

Together with a conversation-identity fix (#106), the end state is: the pill a user saw and
the pill a reviewer sees are provably the same thing, and every conversation a session touched
is actually present in the audit trail.

## The live path: stream → scanner → asides

Today, the model's raw `<citation>` markup streams into the browser DOM, and after the turn
completes, the server sends verdicts over a custom message so `commons-chat.js` can replace
the rendered elements positionally. That final hop is fail-open: until the JS runs (or if it
miscounts), the user is looking at unverified markup dressed as citations.

Now `Commons$stream_async()` wraps every answer in a streaming scanner (`R/citation-scan.R`):

- The model writes a new block dialect, `<commons-citation>` — a short explanation plus a
  blockquote carrying the verbatim excerpt (`inst/prompts/citation-request.md`). The block
  form replaced the old single-line attribute form because it survives streaming: the scanner
  can hold back a partially-arrived block and release everything else immediately.
- Each quote is verified against the same corpus as before (context docs, measure schemas,
  dictionary entries), but mid-stream. Verified citations are rewritten inline as
  `<shiny-aside>` elements naming their source; failed ones are dropped.
- This is fail-closed and unconditional: the scanner runs whether or not tracing is on, the
  dialect never reaches the browser unprojected, and model-spoofed `<shiny-aside>` markup is
  neutralized. Stored turns keep the raw model text — projection is a display concern.
- After the stream, the answer's tag is derived (`derive_provenance_tag()` in
  `R/provenance.R`): governed-tool answers are "A", fallback-tool answers with a verified
  citation "B", without one "C" — same semantics as before, with "B beats A" because the
  citation is the thing the user is being asked to trust. A/C answers get a compact
  provenance aside appended to the stream; a B answer's provenance UI is its citation asides.

Display rides shinychat's aside component, so the custom pill/citation protocol is deleted:
`commons-chat.js` shrinks by ~225 lines, `commons_server()` sends no custom messages, and
`R/tagging.R` (the old post-hoc provenance derivation) is gone entirely.

## The recorded path: spans → trajectory read-back → review

Previously the trajectory viewer *inferred* trust after the fact — tool names implied the tag
(`call_measure` ⇒ verified, `run_sql` ⇒ cited-or-untrusted) and citations were re-scraped from
answer text, with footnotes explicitly labeled "unverified". An inference can disagree with
what the user was actually shown, which is the wrong failure mode for an audit surface.

Now the decisions are recorded where they're made: `stream_async()` writes the tag
(`commons.provenance.tag`) and the scanner's accept/reject decisions
(`commons.citation.candidates`, JSON) onto the `commons_conversation_turn` span.

On the way back out, `trajectory_read()` (`R/trajectory-read.R`) reads those attributes off
every recorded call in a conversation and attaches them per-exchange to the reconstructed
turns. The one genuinely subtle design decision is *how* a recorded call is matched to an
exchange: structurally, by comparing canonicalized exchange-content signatures as a prefix of
the final history — not by ordinal position. Conversation histories aren't append-only once
shinychat's edit and branch-navigation features are in play, so a position recorded by one
call can name the wrong exchange in another call's reality. The comment above
`exchange_signature()` and the provenance block of `test-trajectories.R` (linear, edited,
restored, switched, conflicting, incomplete) are the spec for this; I'd start a review of the
read-back side there.

`trajectory_review()` then becomes a playback device: it reconstructs citation asides from the
stored raw turns using the same scanner, resolved by the *recorded* decisions rather than a
corpus (it never re-verifies), surfaces rejected-citation counts in a review-audit aside, and
takes its pill copy from the same display table the live aside uses so the two can't drift.
Missing or conflicting records fail closed to "no claim" — the viewer never invents a verdict.

## Conversation identity (#106)

While wiring the recorded path I found that shinychat's history feature reuses one client
object across new chats, conversation switches, and edits (all via `set_turns()`), while
commons minted one conversation id per client — so every conversation a session touched shared
one id, and `trajectory_read()`'s latest-span-wins reconstruction silently kept only the last
one. Fixed in two layers (one commit, `R/commons.R` + `R/chat.R`):

- `stream_async()` rotates the conversation id whenever the current turns no longer extend
  the last streamed state.
- `commons_server()` persists the id in each saved conversation's app-state values via
  shinychat's `on_save`/`on_restore` hooks, so reopening a conversation continues under its
  original id instead of duplicating its history under a fresh one. This layer is commented
  as deletable once shinychat records stable conversation identity on its own spans.

## Reviewing guide

- Scanner semantics (hold-back, projection, spoof handling): `R/citation-scan.R`, specced
  exhaustively in `test-citation-scan.R`.
- Recording: `stream_async()` in `R/commons.R`; tag semantics and display table in
  `R/provenance.R`.
- Read-back and structural matching: `R/trajectory-read.R` + the provenance tests in
  `test-trajectories.R`.
- `R/trajectory-review.R` is mostly deletion of the inference path plus playback.
- Real-browser coverage (streaming apps driven via shinytest2/chromote):
  `test-citation-browser.R` and `tests/testthat/apps/` — hence the new Suggests.

## Trade-offs and notes

- **Old traces go dark.** Pre-existing conversations carry no recorded provenance, so they
  show no trust pill in the reviewer. Deliberate: no claim beats an inferred claim, and the
  package's pre-release stance means no compat shims.
- **Read cost grew.** `trajectory_read()` now parses one chat span per recorded exchange
  rather than one per conversation. Fine at review scale; noted in case it ever matters.
- **Abandoned edit branches** are preserved in traces (each under its own id after #106) but
  the reviewer doesn't yet present them as siblings of the edited conversation — tracked as
  the open half of #106.
- Requires shinychat > 0.4.0 for the aside component; adds an R-CMD-check workflow.

title: ci: add package check and address native warning
description:
## Why this matters

This repository did not previously run `R CMD check` in GitHub Actions. The first commit adds that general package gate, and its initial Linux run exposes an existing compiled-code warning from the sandbox capability probe. The following commits remove that warning and stabilize snapshots against a new DuckDB startup notice.

## What changes

- Add a Linux `R CMD check` workflow for the package suite.
- Preserve the probe child's process-wide termination semantics with `SYS_exit_group`, avoiding the libc `_exit` symbol that the compiled-code scan flags.
- Choose DuckDB's temporary test storage home explicitly, preventing its version 1.5.5 startup announcement from changing error snapshots.

## Stacked follow-up

#107 is stacked on this PR. It introduces the browser-test helper, adds `COMMONS_SKIP_BROWSER_TESTS=true` to the inherited package-check workflow, and runs those browser tests in its own dedicated workflow. This PR deliberately contains no citation-specific browser-test policy.

## Verification

- The workflow-only commit reproduced the `_exit` warning on Ubuntu.
- The subsequent run reported `checking compiled code ... OK`.
- `Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "commons")'` passed all affected snapshot assertions locally; its three remaining failures are the known local macOS FTS extension-download block.\n- The previous fresh Linux run passed the package check, deploy, and pkgdown workflows; this branch rewrite has triggered the final standalone rerun.

description:
## Summary
- Adds `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`: sends the app to two Connect servers (dev and staging) using [posit-dev/connect-actions](https://github.com/posit-dev/connect-actions). A push to `main` sends the real, live version. A pull request sends a draft preview instead, and posts a comment with the preview link.
- Adds `.github/workflows/cleanup-previews.yml`: deletes the draft previews from both servers when a pull request closes.
- The two server addresses are stored as GitHub secrets (`CONNECT_SERVER_DEV`, `CONNECT_SERVER_STAGING`) instead of being written directly in the workflow file. This keeps them out of a plain GitHub search. It does **not** fully hide them, though: the deploy step still posts the real address in its pull request comment (see below).
- Login uses Trusted Publishing (OIDC), so no API key is stored. Each app needs a trusted publisher set up for this repo on its Access tab in Connect.
- Fixes the `shinychat` remote in `DESCRIPTION`: the R package actually lives in the `pkg-r` folder of that repo. The old remote pointed at the wrong spot, so it quietly used the CRAN version (0.4.0) instead, which is missing `chat_server`.

The new elements of the semantic layer can only be added to the harness via `data-dict.yaml`  for now and map more readily to the usual semantic layer elements from other vendors. 

The high-trust path now includes one more tool, `query_metrics`, a normal-semantic-layer-shaped analogue to `call_measure`. `search_measures` becomes `search_pool` and searches across the whole pool of vetted computations, both measures and also definition types: `metrics` × `dimensions` × `filters`, each of which can be composed in `query_metrics`.

When there are no measures (like in the devrel-io case) or no governed definitons (like, for now, tiles-agent), the tools and prompting for that part of the agent's harness is removed.

title: Allow the agent to run R code in a sandbox
description:
Set out to tackle data visualizations and ended up tackling a more substantive problem.

Right now, the agent can "post-process" measure output by running SQL against it. This is a bit weird, as 1) the agent needs to know what the measure output looks like before writing the SQL and 2) the thing returned by a measure is an R object.

I had wanted to add support for visualization and had loosely been wondering about:

1) ggsql: Syntactically, can easily be tacked on to the existing SQL implementations, but 
2) ggplot: Hard to give access to ggplot without access to R broadly. Also begs the question of dplyr instead of the existing SQL post-processing. We could allowlist certain functions, but this would probably eventually need to be removed in favor of a more general R tool anyway.
3) A general `run_r` tool. This is what we would need eventually, but sandboxing is hard, deployment is hard, and the combination is hard.

Ended up doing 3), along with removing the existing SQL post-processing interface. Then, each measure and run_sql output gets tagged with a handle s.t. the agent can run code against it in its R session. The R session is a separate process via callr. That process uses Landlock (can only access R libraries and a temp folder) and seccomp (no network) to sandbox the session. Both are unprivileged self-restrictions.

Some inspiration from mcp-repl and btw::run_r.

title: Implement lazy loading for pins
description:
Closes #25. 

Previously, if you used a substantial number of pins as a data source, apps were slow to load because all pins were read into DuckDB tables at startup. 

With this PR, pins are read in lazily:

* `data_source()` with a specified `board` makes a single `pins::pin_list()` call to validate the pin names and returns without reading anything. A pin specified in `data_source()` that isn't in the returned listing triggers a `pins::pin_exists()` check before it's rejected (Connect caps `pins::pin_list()` at 1000 pins). 
* A prewarm feature that downloads as many pins as it can. `commons_server()` starts it during idle time right after startup. The downloads run in a background R process (`callr::r_bg()`) that calls `pins::pin_download()` for each unread pin, so prewarming can't block the main R process. Prewarming only fills the local pins cache. The tables don't get put into DuckDB until they are required (see next bullet), but those reads just parse the cached file and are fast.
*  A pin is read lazily the first time something requires it: a SQL query, the `describe_table` tool, or a measure.
   * For SQL queries, it works by 1) running the SQL the agent requested and 2) if DuckDB returns an error of the type "Table with name [X] does not exist", reading in that pin and retrying. This introduces some latency, but is pretty fast in practice, and is less messy and more correct than name-matching the tables in the SQL. 
   * `describe_table` loads just the one table it inspects. 
   * _Limitation:_ For measures, running a measure loads all of the source's pins, because the tables it queries can't be reliably or easily extracted from the R code. In practice, the hope is that prewarming has already downloaded necessary pins. One reason to keep it this way for now: if measures eventually live in `data-dict.yaml` files with explicit ties to specific tables, we can use those relationships to lazily load just the required pins.

title: feat: instrument commons setup paths with OpenTelemetry spans
description:
This PR adds additional OTEL tracing throughout key actions in commons, with an eye toward adding tracing around time-consuming actions. The goal is to increase traceability to be able to point definitively at (or rule out) areas of commons that need performance tuning.

## Summary

Adds OpenTelemetry tracing across commons' setup paths (not just the Shiny app use case): data source construction (`data_source()`, including connection, board, and in-process DuckDB frame loading), agent construction (`commons()`/`Commons$new()`), context layer indexing (`context_store()` build vs. `prewarm()` cache-hit/miss), and Shiny server startup (`commons_server()`). Spans use a `commons_<snake_case>` naming convention with `commons.<area>.<field>` attributes, are emitted via a new `local_commons_span()` helper in `R/tracing.R` that no-ops when the `otel` package isn't installed, and aren't gated behind the existing `log` (trajectory-logging) flag since they cover setup, not conversation content. `is_installed()` is now statically imported from `staticimports` instead of `rlang`, removing a namespace conflict.

Two issues surfaced by review and fixed before this PR: `commons_agent_create`'s span used to be created before trajectory tracing was configured in `Commons$initialize()`, so it silently bound to a cached no-op tracer and never exported even with `log = TRUE`; the span creation was moved to after tracing setup. Board-backed data sources (`data_source(board, ...)`) used to recursively call the public `data_source()`, producing a duplicate nested `commons_data_source_create` span; frame-loading is now factored into a shared internal `data_source_frames()` helper used by both the top-level frames path and the board path.

## Verification

```r
withr::local_envvar(COMMONS_TRACES_DIR = tempdir())
agent <- commons(
  ellmer::chat_anthropic(),
  data_sources = data_source(sales = data.frame(id = 1:2, revenue = c(100, 200))),
  log = TRUE
)
recorded <- otelsdk::with_otel_record(agent$prewarm())
vapply(recorded$traces, `[[`, character(1), "name")
# shows commons_agent_create, commons_data_source_create, etc.
```

title: Migrate to shinychat's non-module chat API
description:
## Why

shinychat just deprecated its module-based chat API in favor of a simpler,
non-module one: [posit-dev/shinychat#264](https://github.com/posit-dev/shinychat/pull/264).

For background: `chat_mod_ui()`/`chat_mod_server()` required wrapping your
chat in a full Shiny module (`moduleServer()`), which turned out to be more
structure than most apps need — and it obscured the chat's real DOM id behind
private module namespacing, which made things like slash-command JS events
harder to wire up correctly. The replacement, `chat_ui()`/`chat_server()`,
does the same job (streaming, cancellation, bookmarking/history) but runs
directly in the caller's own session — no module required, and no more
hidden id namespacing. It also gets shinychat's new automatic multi-conversation
history for free, which replaces the old manual `bookmark_on_input`/
`bookmark_on_response` flags.

The old functions are only *soft*-deprecated for now (they still work, with a
warning), but there's no reason for us to carry the extra module indirection
now that a simpler, better-supported path exists, and this package hasn't
shipped externally yet — so there's no cost to switching before anyone
depends on the old API.

## What changed

- `commons_mod_ui()`/`commons_mod_server()` → `commons_ui()`/`commons_server()`,
  mirroring shinychat's rename.
- `commons_server()` no longer takes `bookmark_on_input`/`bookmark_on_response`
  — shinychat's `chat_server()` now persists history automatically.
- Fixed a bug this migration would otherwise have introduced: the
  provenance-pill code used to rely on the module's `session$ns()` to
  correctly target the chat's DOM element. Without the module wrapper,
  `session$ns()` no longer does that, so pills were silently failing to
  attach for any chat id other than the literal string `"chat"`. Fixed to
  resolve the id the same way shinychat's own internals do, and added a
  regression test.
- Regenerated docs (`devtools::document()`) so the man pages match the new
  signatures.

## Test plan

- [x] `testthat` suite passes (one pre-existing, unrelated failure in
      `test-citations.R` exists on `main` too)
- [x] Added a test verifying the provenance pill targets the chat's actual id

I know the pins are probably an intermediate solution, but there wasn't a good way to share with them with others. I wanted to share all trajectories from the tiles agent with you and Kelsey.

title: Establish a recommended directory structure, add existing data artifact -> agent implementation skill
Support data dictionaries
description:
Closes #21. `data_source()` gains a `dictionary` argument that, for now, is a path to a data dictionary. From the docs:

> Its content reaches the agent three ways:
> 
> * The dataset-level `description` and `details`, along with the glossary, are included in the system prompt. These fields are the place for rules that span tables and for guidance on which tables answer which kinds of questions.
> * The first time a conversation touches a table---via the `describe_table` tool or a SQL query---the table's full dictionary entry rides along with the tool result: its prose, documented columns, relationships, and definitions of glossary terms it references. `describe_table` merges documented columns with the table's live schema.
> * When the agent also has a `context_layer()`, the dictionary's prose is indexed for the `search_context` tool.

title: Fix scope trap, support multiple data sources
description:
Closes #19.

`commons(data_source)` is now `commons(data_sources)` and accepts a named list of `data_source()`s. If there are many, their name prefixes the selected tables as a header in the system prompt. For `run_sql` and `describe_table`, the model supplies the name of the connection from an enum (measures handle this automatically).

Non-`data_source()` data source should use a normal argument default in the relevant measure's signature.

title: Fix DuckDB connection failure with coexisting connections
description: From Claude (have tested, but not verified in real app). Putting this here in case you have a chance to take a look, otherwise I will test it out later. ## Problem `duckdb_connect()` passed `home_directory` in the DuckDB `config`. But `home_directory` is a process-global, set-at-startup option, so re-setting it on a second connection in the same process fails with: > Could not set option "home_directory" as a global option This happens whenever two DuckDB connections coexist — e.g. the connection `query_measure_output()` opens for SQL post-processing while a data-frame `data_source()` still holds one. The result is that `call_measure(..., sql = ...)` can fail in a long-lived Shiny/Connect app. (On duckdb 1.3.2 the config-with-`home_directory` connect fails on the *first* connection too.) ## Fix - Keep `extension_directory` in `config` — it must be set at startup, before the extension subsystem initializes against the read-only package library on Connect. - Set `home_directory` with a session-scoped `SET home_directory = ...` after connecting, which avoids the global-option conflict and is safe across coexisting connections.

title: derive answers from measure outputs
description:
Closes #4.

Adds an optional `sql` argument to `call_measure` for post-processing tabular measure results through an ephemeral DuckDB scratch connection. This lets the agent build on governed measure outputs for final filters, totals, ratios, and rankings while demoting derived answers to the B trust path.

title: feat: define measures from documented R scripts
description:
## Summary

Adds `read_measures()`, which derives `measure()` definitions from ordinary documented R functions, so a data science team can author governed measures as plain R scripts instead of hand-assembling `measure()` calls.

A function becomes a measure when its roxygen2 block carries a `@measure` tag — much like `@export` marks a function as part of a package's public interface. Its name comes from the function, its description from `@title`/`@description`/`@return`, and its arguments from the `@param` tags. Other documented functions in the file are ignored, so helper functions can live alongside measures. Argument types are declared with a leading code span in the `@param` text — `string`, `integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `enum[...]`, or `type[]` for arrays. An argument is required when its formal has no default; untyped arguments are inferred from their defaults, falling back to string. The code-span syntax was chosen over a bare sigil so the type renders correctly in the generated `.Rd` rather than being mangled by the markdown roclet into a broken `\link{}`.

All files passed in a single `read_measures()` call are sourced in order into one shared environment, so a measure can call helper functions defined in a sibling file of the same call.

`semantic_layer()` now accepts character inputs directly and routes them through `read_measures()`, so file paths, directories, and inline `measure()` objects can be freely mixed in one call (e.g. `semantic_layer("measures.R", my_inline_measure)`). The single-list form continues to work. Separate path arguments stay isolated — `semantic_layer("a.R", "b.R")` reads each file in its own environment, while `semantic_layer(c("a.R", "b.R"))` shares one. One behavior change: a non-path string passed to `semantic_layer()` now errors from `read_measures()` ("Path does not exist") rather than the previous "must be created by `measure()`".

`roxygen2` is added to Suggests, guarded by `rlang::check_installed()` so it is only required when reading measures from scripts. The `@measure` tag is registered at runtime via a `roxy_tag_parse` S3 method (`tag_toggle`), since roxygen2 is only a suggested dependency.

This branch also adopts roxygen2 8.0.0: `DESCRIPTION` records `Config/roxygen2/version: 8.0.0` and the package-level man pages are regenerated to match.

## Verification

```r
# measures.R

#' Count orders
#'
#' @description Total orders, optionally filtered by region and period.
#'
#' @param region `string` The sales region. Omit for all regions.
#' @param period `enum[day, week, month]` Aggregation period.
#' @param top_n `integer` Maximum number of rows to return.
#'
#' @return An integer count of orders.
#' @measure
order_count <- function(region = NULL, period, top_n = 10L) {
  42L
}
```

```r
library(commons)

# Either form works:
sl <- semantic_layer("measures.R")
sl <- semantic_layer(read_measures("measures.R"))

names(sl$measures)
#> [1] "order_count"
```

Full test suite passes (`devtools::test()`, 163 tests), including new coverage for code-span parsing, required-from-signature, default inference, directory and vector inputs, path routing through `semantic_layer()`, the `@measure` opt-in (untagged functions ignored), cross-file helpers via a shared environment, and isolation across separate path arguments.

title: test: close the one-sided gaps in the shared fixture runners
description:
This PR closes the places where only one package's suite checked part of a shared fixture. R now checks `commons_theme()` against `chat-theme.json` and checks that `sendto` is screened only when it has an address. Python now drives the real citation scanner for the decision cases.

Stacked on [posit-dev/commons#487](https://github.com/posit-dev/commons/issues/487).

## R changes

Test-only. R gets a [new runner for the chat theme](https://github.com/posit-dev/commons/pull/488/files#diff-42a2ca16fb6330f1726258004ecbfb1de5979d54f7882d24e2e650d7e99c6056). The [sandbox runner](https://github.com/posit-dev/commons/pull/488/files#diff-246d32f45150caf5c21cd16aea690383f9a91f5b0b7941f4db629fed0d5aaff6) now checks the two groups of screened syscalls separately. The [live-warehouse helper](https://github.com/posit-dev/commons/pull/488/files#diff-c1bd988415d26cf98915fd557e237bdca4f232a9b529e24f66383d0f77aa5266) now skips on any fixture the shared environment marks `required`, where before it hardcoded the schema.

<details><summary>Agent-written notes</summary>

- For [`live-warehouse-rows.json`](https://github.com/posit-dev/commons/pull/488/files#diff-0dec836bbe0db9f96dab4397738de5b9ae3f835f67e3b86cb45fdf9290aebcb7) I corrected the note instead of adding an R runner. The note now says only Python loads the rows into DuckDB. An R DuckDB loader plus a live comparison is a bigger piece of work, and it cannot be verified without warehouse credentials. R's warehouse SQL is still checked against `definition-warehouse-sql.json`.
- `parameterized_model_arguments.format` was read by neither suite, so it is gone. The variable's description already says the value is a JSON object.
- Testing: a mutated sandbox fixture fails the new R checks. Ran ruff, pyrefly, the full pytest suite, and R CMD check.
- kata: bgn3.

</details>

title: fix: refuse an invalid definition with data-dict's problem code
description:
This PR gives each refusal from the local definition exporters the data-dict problem code it matches (`S21`, `S34`, ...). Both suites now check the code that `definitions.json` pins for each invalid fixture. Before, any error passed every case.

Stacked on [posit-dev/commons#486](https://github.com/posit-dev/commons/issues/486).

## R changes

Refusals in [`definition-export.R`](https://github.com/posit-dev/commons/pull/487/files#diff-9adee9131e07b24a90ac743391ec8ee1d97ed1eaeb39d16944743021cabecbae) now signal `commons_definition_invalid_error` with a `code` field. The same inputs are refused. One message changes: a `COLUMNS(...)` filter over non-boolean columns now opens with the "does not type-check" line that other type errors use. A type-check failure keeps the code of the inner error (`S20` for an unknown column, `S30` for a nested aggregate) and otherwise reports `S21`.

<details><summary>Agent-written notes</summary>

- One class plus a `code` attribute, where [posit-dev/commons#436](https://github.com/posit-dev/commons/issues/436) used one class per refusal, because the fixture already uses data-dict's codes. In Python it is `DefinitionInvalidError`, a `ValueError` subclass ([`_export.py`](https://github.com/posit-dev/commons/pull/487/files#diff-54a040d9f7b725b5512dad136c3eff6982e04a080adbf1e5c6f5d8c80dee082e)).
- Codes for refusals the corpus did not cover came from the pinned binary. Four new invalid fixtures pin four of them: a missing struct field, a duplicate column, a missing column in a `COLUMNS([...])` list, and a `COLUMNS(...)` filter over non-boolean columns. Schema-shape problems, such as a non-string label, stay plain errors, because data-dict reports them as schema errors, not problem codes.
- Also here: the Python runner now compares the whole DuckDB translation, including `error`, as the R runner already did.
- Testing: a mutated code fails both runners. Ran ruff, pyrefly, the full pytest suite, and R CMD check. The R suite's comparison with the installed data-dict binary passes for the two new fixtures.
- kata: 438r.

</details>

title: Replace the `pull_request_target` fork notice with a docs-build annotation
description:
Closes [posit-dev/commons#489](https://github.com/posit-dev/commons/issues/489).

This PR removes our only `pull_request_target` workflow, which GitHub will block from December 2, 2026. The Python docs build now tells fork authors that they get no preview, in a run annotation and summary instead of a PR comment.

title: fix: type a NULL that a temporal shift reaches through a sibling definition
description:
This PR fixes a definition like `created + n` when the sibling definition `n` is always NULL. It used to compose to `"created" + (NULL)`, which Snowflake refuses. Both packages now replace a reference to an always-NULL sibling with the NULL itself, so the typed-NULL rule from [posit-dev/commons#444](https://github.com/posit-dev/commons/issues/444) applies.

Stacked on [posit-dev/commons#437](https://github.com/posit-dev/commons/issues/437).

## R changes

Binding in [`definition-compile.R`](https://github.com/posit-dev/commons/pull/486/files#diff-29b2204ccc225ac88ddcc4ab5f1608b4040a83d5c8a8c749be5d25d2bbf8f68a) now works out which definitions on a table are always NULL: a bare NULL, or a reference to one, followed to any depth. A reference to such a definition is emitted as NULL. A date shifted by such a definition now compiles to `CAST(NULL AS TIMESTAMP_TZ)` on Snowflake and `CAST(NULL AS TIMESTAMP)` on Databricks, where it used to be `"created" + (NULL)`. The SQL for other definitions is unchanged.

<details><summary>Agent-written notes</summary>

- The shared corpus ([`language.yaml`](https://github.com/posit-dev/commons/pull/486/files#diff-d68889ccd174c1033da26ef3753456137dac83108f6369f16ac8026bac6c4f35)) gains three definitions: `absent offset`, `relayed offset`, and `date shifted by a null sibling`. They go through a relay so the chained case is covered. `export_records` was regenerated from the pinned binary, `composed` and `mixed_grain` were added by hand, and the corpus counts in both suites went from 42 to 45.
- Testing: each fixture case fails without the fix in both packages. Ran ruff, `pyrefly check src tests`, the full pytest suite, and R CMD check (with `_R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_=false`, because `rsconnect` and `RSQLite` are not installed locally).
- kata: y8nf.

</details>

title: cap describe_table column output
description: Closes #475. `describe_table` now shows at most 50 columns and reports how many were omitted, covering documented and undocumented tables. Both R and Python.

title: feat(py): grant Connect users access to recorded trajectories
description:
This PR adds `share_trajectory_access()` to the Python Connect client. The function gives named Connect users the collaborator role on the content, so that they can read its trajectories. Nothing calls it yet. It also fixes R's `share_with`, which skipped users who could already view the app. Stacked on [posit-dev/commons#252](https://github.com/posit-dev/commons/issues/252).

<details>
<summary>Design notes (agent-written)</summary>

- The new `collaborator_grant` and `sharing` sections in [`connect.json`](https://github.com/posit-dev/commons/pull/478/files#diff-7b9773fb688edd027c2047bccef8229b79bda1bc3ca9a00cde9330249950c845) specify what a grant does. Both suites read them.
- Connect's permissions API names the role that can read traces "owner", and it rejects "editor".
- A failed grant gives a warning instead of an error, because a grant must not stop the agent from being built. This applies to a Connect outage and to a response that commons cannot read. A `usernames` value that is not a sequence of strings still raises `TypeError`.
- Each process records the (content, username) pairs that it has granted. When an agent is built again, it does not send the same requests again.
- kata: `8t5y`. The Python `share_with` argument comes with the agent-facing tracing setup (`cyyz`/`w0t2`).
</details>

## R changes

[`share_trajectory_access()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/commons/pull/478/files#diff-e67cdaf0a70c973f063837c77b18890fb796efd028ac78560c4267c2bb077cd3) skipped every user who had any permission on the content. As a result, a user with only viewer access did not get the grant and still could not read the traces. [`connect_collaborator_principals()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/commons/pull/478/files#diff-a1b13721b044c31683af0d34b8fc5e21a14e8f774a0758bdba7dbb2ce34026f0) now counts only the "owner" role, so these users get the grant. There is a NEWS bullet for this change. `share_with` now also changes usernames to lowercase and removes duplicates before it looks them up, because Connect ignores case in usernames. If the permissions response is a JSON object instead of a list, `share_with` now gives a warning. Before, it read that response as "nobody has access" and granted access to everyone named. The tests now get their cases from the shared fixture.

title: ci(r): use the main Ubuntu archive for apt, and time out stalled jobs
ci(r): check R-devel only off pull requests, and weekly
description:
This PR stops running the R-devel check on pull requests. It still runs on pushes to `main`, on manual dispatch, and on a new weekly schedule.

R-devel has no binary packages, so when its cache misses, the job compiles about 155 dependencies from source and takes 20 minutes or more. The cache misses on nearly every pull request: at 583 MB it is the largest cache in the repository, and the 10 GB limit evicts caches within hours. The cost is that a problem only R-devel shows appears after a merge rather than before it.

The devel job shares its steps with the main check through a YAML anchor, so the two cannot drift apart.

title: fix(py): keep NaN in Databricks query results
description:
This PR makes commons keep `NaN` in query results from a Databricks engine. Before, the Databricks connector changed each `NaN` double to `None`, so an answer such as `inf + -inf` read as `NULL`.

[`EngineBackend.query`](https://github.com/posit-dev/commons/pull/474/files#diff-0f8e777d6aa8ead17a0c1afbff724be3a12b8758eb147bba2568fa748784553d) now reads a Databricks engine's rows from the connector's Arrow result. Other dialects do not change. This also changes two other things on Databricks: array columns come back as lists, not numpy arrays, and a failed query raises the connector's own exception, not SQLAlchemy's wrapper. The access-error classifier already reads both.

<details>
<summary>Testing (agent-written)</summary>

- The Python checks pass (ruff, pyrefly, pytest).
- I compared the old and new paths against a live Databricks workspace. `NaN` is kept, and all other values are the same, apart from arrays now being lists. Access probes still classify a denied table as an authorization refusal.
- This PR adds no unit test, because only a real Databricks connection shows the problem. The live comparison in #434 (`values::numeric`) fails without this fix.
- kata: whhh

</details>
